TASK task_0001 — Write ONE file: C:\kamlesh\test\games\zombie3\js\textures.js

CONTEXT
- Three.js r128 is already at C:\kamlesh\test\games\zombie3\three.min.js, loaded via <script src="three.min.js"></script> before your file. Global `THREE` exists at runtime (r128 legacy API: `new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas)`, `THREE.sRGBEncoding`, `THREE.RepeatWrapping`, `THREE.LinearMipmapLinearFilter` are all valid).
- The game runs from file:// (no server) so NO fetch, NO external files/URLs, NO ES modules. Classic script only, must not use `module`, `export`, `import`.
- Your file is loaded BEFORE world.js / zombie.js / weapons.js.

REQUIREMENTS
1. Define a single global `const Z3Tex = { ... }` (assign with `var Z3Tex = { ... };` at top level so it becomes a global; also do `window.Z3Tex = Z3Tex;` at the end for safety).
2. Deterministic seeded RNG inside the module (e.g. `mulberry32`); never use Math.random for texture content so textures are stable between reloads.
3. Canvas size default 512 (never above 512). Provide helpers:
   - `Z3Tex.makeCanvas(size)` -> {canvas, ctx}
   - `Z3Tex.valueNoise(size, freq, seed)` and `Z3Tex.fbm(size, opts)` -> Float32Array/2D height data
   - `Z3Tex.normalMapFromHeight(canvas, strength)` -> THREE.CanvasTexture containing a proper tangent-space normal map computed with a Sobel filter from the luminance of the given canvas (R,G,B encoded as (n*0.5+0.5)*255). Set wrapS/wrapT = THREE.RepeatWrapping.
   - `Z3Tex.grain(ctx, size, amount)` noise overlay helper, `Z3Tex.stains(...)`, `Z3Tex.cracks(...)` helpers as needed.
4. Each material factory returns an object shaped EXACTLY like:
   `{ map: THREE.CanvasTexture, normalMap: THREE.CanvasTexture, roughness: <number 0..1>, metalness: <number 0..1> }`
   All maps must have `wrapS = wrapT = THREE.RepeatWrapping`, `anisotropy = 1`, and generated mipmaps (`generateMipmaps` default true), `map.encoding = THREE.sRGBEncoding` for color maps (normal maps must stay linear, i.e. do NOT set sRGBEncoding on normalMap).
5. Memoize every factory (same name -> same cached object) so repeated calls are cheap. Add `Z3Tex.dispose()` that disposes all cached textures.
6. Required factories (all must look convincing, gritty, desaturated post-apocalyptic, not flat colors):
   - `asphalt()` cracked grey asphalt road with patches, oil stains, small stones
   - `roadLine()` asphalt with a faded white/yellow dashed lane marking baked in (tileable along the road direction)
   - `sidewalk()` concrete slabs with expansion joint lines, gum stains, cracks
   - `concrete()` dirty poured-concrete wall, water streaks, chipped edges
   - `plaster()` aged plaster/mortar wall with erosion and grime
   - `brick()` running-bond red/brown bricks with mortar and soot
   - `wood()` weathered wooden planks with grain, knots and nail holes
   - `metal()` brushed/scratched galvanised metal panels
   - `rustMetal()` heavy rust + pitted metal (for barrels, dumpsters, decaying cars)
   - `carPaint(hexColor)` coloured car body with clearcoat scratches, dust and rust spots
   - `dirt()` bare compacted dirt / gravel ground with footprints-ish blotches
   - `grassDry()` dead dry grass tufts over dirt
   - `bark()` tree bark vertical ridges (dead tree)
   - `roof()` gravel/tar roof or corrugated metal roof
   - `windowGrid()` dark building facade glass: dark reflective panes in a grid with a few broken/shattered panes; also returns `emissive` THREE.CanvasTexture where most panes are black but ~6-10% panes glow dim warm/cold (dead streetlight / survivor lamp) - include the extra property `emissive` in the returned object for this factory only
   - `bloodSplat()` soft dark-red blood splatter with drips and a transparent background (canvas must use alpha; return `{map, normalMap: null, roughness: 0.35, metalness: 0}` for data consistency, and the map must have `transparent: true` friendly alpha)
   - `bloodPool()` large irregular dried blood pool with darker edge
   - `crate()` wooden shipping crate with stencil markings and dirt
   - `fleshSkin(tint)` zombie skin, mottled decayed tones with bruised/vascular patches and small wounds (unused areas must still look good tiled on small body parts)
   - `cloth(tint)` torn dirty cloth with holes and dirt gradient
   - `bulletHole()` small dark bullet-hole decal with cracks (transparent background, alpha), used for decals
   - `poster()` torn/peeling warning poster ("QUARANTINE"/"DANGER" blocks and red tape), text can be abstract blocks - no external fonts, draw only rectangles/lines/shapes
   - `sign()` weathered metal street/road sign texture, dark green/white abstract shapes
   - `tileFloor()` dirty ceramic tiles with grout for building interiors
   Keep a shared internal palette of desaturated greys/browns/greens; avoid saturated cartoon colors.
7. Performance: each factory must build at most ~3 canvases and must not take more than ~40 ms. Do not create CanvasTextures at module load time; only when a factory is first called (lazy). Everything must be safe to call before the DOM is fully ready but assume `document` exists.
8. Style: vanilla ES2017, no libraries, ~2-space indent, comments in English, functions short and readable. Keep the file under ~700 lines. Do NOT create any other file and do NOT modify any other file.

VERIFY BEFORE REPORTING (required)
Run: `node --check C:\kamlesh\test\games\zombie3\js\textures.js` and paste the output. Also run a headless logic smoke test with a tiny THREE/document stub if you can (optional, e.g. `node -e "..."` with a stub for document.createElement('canvas') using a minimal object) - if a stub is too complex, at minimum confirm `node --check` passes and list every exported factory name.

Report: status, absolute file path, line count, the exact list of factories, and the `node --check` result.
I'll start by exploring the workspace to understand existing conventions before writing the file.
